questions.prompt: An agent fixed the function you asked about, ran the test suite, reported success — and the reported bug is still reproducible. Which link in the loop broke?
options: Verification — the checks it ran could not have detected the bug
Capability — the model is not strong enough to fix this class of bug
Surface — it needed a tool it did not have
Context — it never saw the file containing the bug
questions.explanation: The agent read files, made an edit, and reported honestly — the loop ran correctly. What it could not do was detect the failure, so a green suite proved nothing. Option B and C are ruled out by the report itself: a capability gap would have shown as an admission, and a missing tool would have surfaced as flailing. Option D is possible but would usually produce a confident wrong answer about the code rather than a plausible edit plus a green run.

questions.prompt: You ask an agent to find every caller of a function in a path it cannot see. It returns a confident list anyway. What actually happened?
options: The model retrieved the answer from training data about your project
The system prompt overrode your request and sent it to a different model
An empty tool result was treated as evidence of absence, so the model generated the callers
The context window dropped your request before the search ran
questions.explanation: The search returned nothing, and nothing is not 'these do not exist' — it is 'I looked in the wrong place'. Treating it as absence let the model fall back on generation, which is exactly what Lesson 6 describes. Option A is the misconception this phase exists to kill: the model has no access to your repo except through tools. Option D would produce a missing-search symptom, not a confident answer.

questions.prompt: The agent is three steps into a search you know is heading the wrong way. You want to redirect it without losing the work already done. What do you do?
options: Press Esc to stop it, then start the session over with better instructions
Type the correction and press Enter without stopping
Wait for it to finish, then correct it in the next message
Run /rewind to restore every file it has changed
questions.explanation: A typed correction is queued and picked up as soon as the current tool calls finish, so the redirect happens without discarding the work already done. Option A throws away the work to buy a cleaner start, which is almost never worth it mid-investigation. Option C works but costs the wasted steps. Option D is a file restore, not a conversation steering tool — it undoes edits, not a wrong search.
